0 # lazygit

A simple terminal UI for git commands. ## Description Lazygit is a terminal UI for git commands that makes working with git easier and more intuitive. Instead of typing complex git commands, you can use a simple visual interface to perform common git operations. ## Features ### Stage individual lines Press space on the selected line to stage it, or press `v` to start selecting a range of lines. You can also press `a` to select the entirety of the current hunk. ### Interactive Rebase Press `i` to start an interactive rebase. Then squash (`s`), fixup (`f`), drop (`d`), edit (`e`), move up (`ctrl+k`) or move down (`ctrl+j`) any of TODO commits, before continuing the rebase by bringing up the rebase options menu with `m` and then selecting `continue`. ### Cherry-pick Press `shift+c` on a commit to copy it and press `shift+v` to paste (cherry-pick) it. ### Bisect Press `b` in the commits view to mark a commit as good/bad in order to begin a git bisect. ### Nuke the working tree For when you really want to just get rid of anything that shows up when you run `git status`, press `shift+d` to bring up the reset options menu and then select the 'nuke' option. ### Amend an old commit Pressing `shift+a` on any commit will amend that commit with the currently staged changes (running an interactive rebase in the background). ### Filter You can filter a view with `/`. For example, filter down the branches view and then hit `enter` to view its commits. ### Worktrees You can create worktrees to have multiple branches going at once without the need for stashing or creating WIP commits when switching between them. Press `w` in the branches view to create a worktree from the selected branch and switch to it. ### Undo Lazygit provides powerful undo capabilities. See the documentation for details. ### Commit graph Lazygit displays a visual commit graph showing the relationship between commits. ## Installation Lazygit is available through various package managers: ### Binary Releases Download pre-built binaries from the releases page. ### Homebrew (macOS and Linux) ```sh brew install lazygit ``` ### MacPorts (macOS) ```sh sudo port install lazygit ``` ### Scoop (Windows) ```sh scoop install lazygit ``` ### Chocolatey (Windows) ```sh choco install lazygit ``` ### Winget (Windows) ```sh winget install -e --id=JesseDuffield.lazygit ``` ### Arch Linux ```sh sudo pacman -S lazygit ``` ### Fedora / CentOS Stream ```sh sudo dnf install lazygit ``` ### Debian and Ubuntu ```sh sudo apt install lazygit ``` ### NixOS ```sh nix-env -iA nixpkgs.lazygit ``` ### FreeBSD ```sh pkg install lazygit ``` ### Conda ```sh conda install -c conda-forge lazygit ``` And many other package managers. Check your system's package manager for availability. ## Usage Call `lazygit` in your terminal inside a git repository: ```sh $ lazygit ``` You can also add an alias for convenience: ```sh echo "alias lg='lazygit'" >> ~/.zshrc ``` ### Changing Directory On Exit If you change repos in lazygit and want your shell to change directory into that repo on exiting lazygit, add this to your `~/.zshrc` (or other rc file): ```sh lg() { export LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE=~/.lazygit/newdir lazygit "$@" if [ -f $LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE ]; then cd "$(cat $LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE)" rm -f $LAZYGIT_NEW_DIR_FILE > /dev/null fi } ``` Then `source ~/.zshrc` and from now on when you call `lg` and exit you'll switch directories to whatever you were in inside lazygit. To override this behaviour you can exit using `shift+Q` rather than just `q`. ## Configuration ### Config File Location Default path for the config file: - Linux: `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml` - MacOS: `~/Library/Application Support/lazygit/config.yml` - Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lazygit\config.yml` You can create repo-specific config files in `/.git/lazygit.yml`. Settings in these files override settings in the global config file. ### Keybindings Lazygit provides extensive keyboard shortcuts for all operations. See the keybindings documentation for a complete list. ### Custom Commands Lazygit has a flexible custom command system that allows you to extend its functionality with your own commands. ## Documentation For more detailed documentation, see the `docs/` directory, which includes: - Configuration guide (Config.md) - Custom command keybindings (Custom_Command_Keybindings.md) - Custom pagers (Custom_Pagers.md) - Undo/Redo functionality (Undoing.md) - And more ## FAQ ### What do the commit colors represent? - Green: The local commit is not yet on the remote - Yellow: The commit is on both local and remote - Red: The local commit is not on the remote but the remote has commits that the local doesn't ## License See LICENSE file for details.

actions.command:
cat > /tmp/cap.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: cap.sh <session> [count] [-e]
S=$1; N=${2:-45}
tmux capture-pane -t $S -p -e | head -$N | sed -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[a-zA-Z]//g' > /tmp/cap.$S.txt
cat /tmp/cap.$S.txt
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/cap.sh
cd /tmp/repo1 && tmux capture-pane -t lg1 -p -e | head -3 | sed 's/\x1b/<ESC>/g'

# User Config

Default path for the global config file:

- Linux: `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml`
- MacOS: `~/Library/Application\ Support/lazygit/config.yml`
- Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lazygit\config.yml` (default location, but it will also be found in `%APPDATA%\lazygit\config.yml`

For old installations (slightly embarrassing: I didn't realise at the time that you didn't need to supply a vendor name to the path so I just used my name):

- Linux: `~/.config/jesseduffield/lazygit/config.yml`
- MacOS: `~/Library/Application\ Support/jesseduffield/lazygit/config.yml`
- Windows: `%APPDATA%\jesseduffield\lazygit\config.yml`

If you want to change the config directory:

- MacOS: `export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`

In addition to the global config file you can create repo-specific config files in `<repo>/.git/lazygit.yml`. Settings in these files override settings in the global config file. In addition, files called `.lazygit.yml` in any of the parent directories of a repo will also be loaded; this can be useful if you have settings that you want to apply to a group of repositories.

JSON schema is available for `config.yml` so that IntelliSense in Visual Studio Code (completion and error checking) is automatically enabled when the [YAML Red Hat][yaml] extension is installed. However, note that automatic schema detection only works if your config file is in one of the standard paths mentioned above. If you override the path to the file, you can still make IntelliSense work by adding

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/master/schema/config.json
```

to the top of your config file or via [Visual Studio Code settings.json config][settings].

[yaml]: https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=redhat.vscode-yaml
[settings]: https://github.com/redhat-developer/vscode-yaml#associating-a-schema-to-a-glob-pattern-via-yamlschemas

## Default

This is only meant as a reference for what config options exist, and what their default values are. It is not meant to be copied and pasted into your config file as a whole; that's not a good idea for several reasons. It is recommended to include only those settings in your config file that you actually want to change.

gui:

  scrollHeight: 2

  scrollPastBottom: true

==== pager
1:# Custom Pagers
2-
3:Lazygit supports custom pagers, [configured](/docs/Config.md) in the config.yml file (which can be opened by pressing `e` in the Status panel).
4-
5-Support does not extend to Windows users, because we're making use of a package which doesn't have Windows support. However, see [below](#emulating-custom-pagers-on-windows) for a workaround.
6-
7-Multiple pagers are supported; you can cycle through them with the `|` key. This can be useful if you usually prefer a particular pager, but want to use a different one for certain kinds of diffs.
8-
9-Pagers are configured with the `pagers` array in the git section; here's an example for a multi-pager setup:
10-
11-```yaml
12-git:
13-  pagers:
14-    - pager: delta --dark --paging=never
15-    - pager: ydiff -p cat -s --wrap --width={{columnWidth}}
16-      colorArg: never
17-    - externalDiffCommand: difft --color=always
18-```
19-
20-The `colorArg` key is for whether you want the `--color=always` arg in your `git diff` command. Some pagers want it set to `always`, others want it set to `never`. The default is `always`, since that's what most pagers need.
21-
22-## Delta:
23-
24-```yaml
25-git:
26-  pagers:
27-    - pager: delta --dark --paging=never
28-```

95:There is a trick to emulate custom pagers on Windows using a Powershell script configured as an external diff command. It's not perfect, but certainly better than nothing. To do this, save the following script as `lazygit-pager.ps1` at a convenient place on your disk:

98-#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
99-
100-$old = $args[1].Replace('\', '/')
101-$new = $args[4].Replace('\', '/')
102-$path = $args[0]
103-git diff --no-index --no-ext-diff $old $new
104-  | %{ $_.Replace($old, $path).Replace($new, $path) }
105-  | delta --width=$env:LAZYGIT_COLUMNS

	UserConfigPaths []string
	Debug         bool
	WriteToDebug bool
}

func ConfigDir() string {
	xdgConfigHome := os.Getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
	if xdgConfigHome == "" {
		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
		xdgConfigHome = filepath.Join(home, ".config")
	}
	return filepath.Join(xdgConfigHome, "lazygit")
}

func StateDir() string {
	xdgStateHome := os.Getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME")
	if xdgStateHome == "" {
		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
		xdgStateHome = filepath.Join(home, ".local", "state")
	}
	return filepath.Join(xdgStateHome, "lazygit")
}

func CacheDir() string {
	xdgCacheHome := os.Getenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME")
	if xdgCacheHome == "" {
		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
		xdgCacheHome = filepath.Join(home, ".cache")
	}
	return filepath.Join(xdgCacheHome, "lazygit")
}

// LoadUserConfig loads the user config files (in order) onto the default config.
func LoadUserConfig(paths []string) (*UserConfig, error) {
	userConfig := UserConfigDefaults()
	for _, path := range paths {
		if path == "" {
			continue
		}
		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err != nil {
			continue
		}
		content, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		node, err := DecodeYAML(string(content))
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		applyYAMLToConfig(userConfig, node)
	}
	return userConfig, nil
}

// splitCommut separates a comma separated list, honouring escaped commas.
func splitCommut(s string) []string {
	if s == "" {
		return nil
	}
	return strings.Split(s, ",")
}

import re,subprocess
def run(K,H):
    subprocess.run(['git','checkout','-q','--','.'],cwd='/tmp/repo1')
    open('/tmp/repo1/a.txt','w').write('\n'.join('line%d'%i for i in range(1,K+1))+'\n')
    dl=int(subprocess.run(['git','diff'],cwd='/tmp/repo1',capture_output=True).stdout.count(b'\n'))
    subprocess.run(['bash','/tmp/exp3.sh','120',str(H),'','/tmp/repo1'],capture_output=True)
    lines=[re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',l) for l in open('/tmp/exp_out.txt').read().split('\n')]
    cmdtop=None
    for i,l in enumerate(lines,1):
        if len(l)>41 and l[40]=='\u256d' and 'Command log' in l: cmdtop=i
    thumb=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines,1) if i<cmdtop and len(l)>119 and l[119]=='\u2590']
    print("K=%3d C=%3d H=%d mainRows=1..%d thumbRows=%d..%d (n=%d)"%(K,dl+1,H,cmdtop-1,thumb[0],thumb[-1],len(thumb)))
for h in [40,60,80,100,120]:
    run(40,h)

import re,subprocess,math
def run(K,H=40):
    subprocess.run(['git','checkout','-q','--','.'],cwd='/tmp/repo1')

	FilesContext      ContextKey = "files"
	WorktreesContext  ContextKey = "worktrees"
	SubmodulesContext ContextKey = "submodules"
	StagingContext    ContextKey = "staging"
	PatchBuildingContext ContextKey = "patchBuilding"
	MergeConflictsContext ContextKey = "mergeConflicts"
	BranchesContext   ContextKey = "branches"
	RemotesContext    ContextKey = "remotes"
	TagsContext       ContextKey = "tags"
	CommitsContext    ContextKey = "commits"
	ReflogContext     ContextKey = "reflog"
	StashContext      ContextKey = "stash"
	CommitFilesContext ContextKey = "commitFiles"
	MainContext       ContextKey = "main"
	SearchingContext  ContextKey = "search"
	GlobalContext     ContextKey = "global"
	InformationContext ContextKey = "information"
	ConfirmationContext ContextKey = "confirmation"
	MenuContext       ContextKey = "menu"
	CommitMessageContext ContextKey = "commitMessage"
	CommitDescriptionContext ContextKey = "commitDescription"
	ExtrasContext     ContextKey = "extras"
)

// Context is a panel view with its keybindings and content.
type Context struct {
	Key    ContextKey
	Window int // index of the side panel window; -1 for main views
	Tab    int
	Title  string // tab title
	View   string // view name
	// rendering
	GetLines   func() []Line
	GetFooter  func() string
	// main view
	MainTitle   func() string
	MainContent func() []Line
	// keybindings
	Keybindings []Keybinding
	// whether this context can be focused
	Focusable bool
	// index within the window (for tab ordering)
}

// SideWindow describes a panel of the side bar.
type SideWindow struct {
	Name      string
	JumpKey   string
	Contexts  []*Context
}

// GlobalWindows are the side panels in order.
func SideWindows() []*SideWindow {
	return []*SideWindow{
		{Name: "status", JumpKey: "1", Contexts: []*Context{}},
		{Name: "files", JumpKey: "2", Contexts: []*Context{}},
		{Name: "branches", JumpKey: "3", Contexts: []*Context{}},
		{Name: "commits", JumpKey: "4", Contexts: []*Context{}},
		{Name: "stash", JumpKey: "5", Contexts: []*Context{}},
	}
}
GOEOF

// optionsText returns the text of the bottom line.
func (gui *Gui) optionsText() string {
	if p := gui.TopPopup(); p != nil {
		if len(p.DisabledOptions) > 0 {
			return "Disabled: " + strings.Join(p.DisabledOptions, ", ") + " " + p.Options
		}
		return p.Options
	}
	ctx := gui.CurrentContext()
	if gui.CurrentContextKey == MainContext {
		return "Switch view: <tab> | Exit back to side panel: <esc> | Keybindings: ?"
	}
	switch ctx.Key {
	case StatusContext:
		return "Edit config file: e | Check for update: u | Switch to a recent repo: <enter> | Keybindings: ?"
	case FilesContext:
		if len(gui.StatusFiles) > 0 {
			return "Stage: <space> | Commit: c | Edit: e | Stash: s | Discard: d | Reset: D | Keybindings: ?"
		}
		return "Commit: c | Stash: s | Reset: D | Keybindings: ?"
	case WorktreesContext:
		return "New worktree: n | Switch: <space> | Remove: d | Keybindings: ?"
	case SubmodulesContext:
		return "Enter: <enter> | Remove: d | Update: u | New submodule: n | Keybindings: ?"
	case BranchesContext:
		return "Checkout: <space> | New branch: n | Delete: d | Rebase: r | Reset: g | Upstream: u | Keybindings: ?"
	case RemotesContext:
		return "View branches: <enter> | New remote: n | Remove: d | Edit: e | Fetch: f | Add fork remote: F | Keybindings: ?"
	case TagsContext:
		return "Checkout: <space> | New tag: n | Delete: d | Push tag: P | Reset: g | Keybindings: ?"
	case CommitsContext:
		return "Reword: r | Drop: d | Edit: e | Amend: A | Checkout: <space> | Reset: g | Copy (cherry-pick): C | Keybindings: ?"
	case ReflogContext:
		return "Checkout: <space> | Reset: g | Copy (cherry-pick): C | Keybindings: ?"
	case StashContext:
		return "Apply: <space> | Pop: g | Drop: d | Keybindings: ?"
	}
	return "Keybindings: ?"
}

// showKeybindingsMenu displays the keybindings menu for the current context.
func (gui *Gui) showKeybindingsMenu() error {
	ctx := gui.CurrentContext()
	var lines []Line
	lines = append(lines, NewLine("--- "+ctx.Title+" ---"))
	kbs := gui.keybindingsFor(ctx.Key)
	sort.SliceStable(kbs, func(i, j int) bool { return kbs[i].Key < kbs[j].Key })
	for _, b := range kbs {
		key := b.Key
		if len(key) < 7 {
			key = strings.Repeat(" ", 7-len(key)) + key
		}
		desc := b.Description
		if b.Handler == nil {
			desc += "..."
		}
		lines = append(lines, NewLine(key+" "+desc))
	}
	for _, l := range gui.universalKeybindingList() {
		lines = append(lines, NewLine(l))
	}
	gui.ShowPopup(Popup{
		Title:  "Keybindings",
		Lines:  lines,
		Options: "Execute: <enter> | Close/Cancel: <esc>",
		DisabledOptions: []string{"No item selected"},
	})
	return nil
}

// showKeybindingsMenu displays the keybindings menu for the current context.
func (gui *Gui) showKeybindingsMenu() error {
	ctx := gui.CurrentContext()
	var lines []Line
	lines = append(lines, NewLine("--- "+ctx.Title+" ---"))
	kbs := gui.keybindingsFor(ctx.Key)
	sort.SliceStable(kbs, func(i, j int) bool { return kbs[i].Key < kbs[j].Key })
	for _, b := range kbs {
		key := b.Key
		if len(key) < 7 {
			key = strings.Repeat(" ", 7-len(key)) + key
		}
		desc := b.Description
		if b.Handler == nil {
			desc += "..."
		}
		lines = append(lines, NewLine(key+" "+desc))
	}
	for _, l := range gui.universalKeybindingList() {
		lines = append(lines, NewLine(l))
	}
	gui.ShowPopup(Popup{
		Title:  "Keybindings",
		Lines:  lines,
		Options: "Execute: <enter> | Close/Cancel: <esc>",
		DisabledOptions: []string{"No item selected"},
	})
	return nil
}

// showKeybindingsMenu displays the keybindings menu for the current context.
func (gui *Gui) showKeybindingsMenu() error {
	ctx := gui.CurrentContext()
	var lines []Line
	lines = append(lines, NewLine("--- "+ctx.Title+" ---"))
	kbs := gui.keybindingsFor(ctx.Key)
	sort.SliceStable(kbs, func(i, j int) bool { return kbs[i].Key < kbs[j].Key })
	for _, b := range kbs {
		key := b.Key
		if len(key) < 7 {
			key = strings.Repeat(" ", 7-len(key)) + key
		}
		desc := b.Description
		if b.Handler == nil {
			desc += "..."
		}
		lines = append(lines, NewLine(key+" "+desc))
	}
	for _, l := range gui.universalKeybindingList() {
		lines = append(lines, NewLine(l))
	}
	gui.ShowPopup(Popup{
		Title:  "Keybindings",
		Lines:  lines,
		Options: "Execute: <enter> | Close/Cancel: <esc>",
		DisabledOptions: []string{"No item selected"},
	})
	return nil
}

// showExtrasMenu displays the command log options.
func (gui *Gui) showExtrasMenu() error {
	lines := []Line{
		NewLine("--- Command log ---"),
		NewLine("        Toggle the command log: '@'"),
		NewLine("        Hide the command log: 'h'"),
	}
	gui.ShowPopup(Popup{
		Title:   "Command log options",
		Lines:   lines,
		Options: "Execute: <enter> | Close/Cancel: <esc>",
		DisabledOptions: []string{"No item selected"},
	})
	return nil
}

// showRecentRepos displays the recent repos menu.
func (gui *Gui) showRecentRepos() error {
	repos := gui.AppState.RecentRepos
	var lines []Line
	if len(repos) == 0 {
		lines = append(lines, NewLine("No recent repositories"))
	}
	for _, r := range repos {
		lines = append(lines, NewLine(r))
	}
	gui.ShowPopup(Popup{
		Title:  "Recent repos",
		Lines:  lines,
		Options: "Execute: <enter> | Close/Cancel: <esc>",
		DisabledOptions: []string{"No item selected"},
	})
	return nil
}

func (gui *Gui) fileTreeLines() []Line {
	files := gui.StatusFiles
	if len(files) == 0 {
		return []Line{}
	}
	sorted := make([]commands.StatusFile, len(files))
	copy(sorted, files)
	sort.SliceStable(sorted, func(i, j int) bool { return sorted[i].Name < sorted[j].Name })
	gui.StatusFiles = sorted

	type node struct {
		name     string
		isDir    bool
		children []*node
		expanded bool
		file     *commands.StatusFile
	}
	root := &node{name: "", isDir: true, expanded: true}
	index := map[string]*node{"": root}
	for i := range gui.StatusFiles {
		f := &gui.StatusFiles[i]
		parts := strings.Split(f.Name, "/")
		cur := root
		path := ""
		for pi, p := range parts {
			last := pi == len(parts)-1
			if path == "" {
				path = p
			} else {
				path = path + "/" + p
			}
			if last {

					index[path] = n
					cur.children = append(cur.children, n)
				}
				cur = n
			}
		}
	}

		}
		for i, c := range n.children {
			n.children[i] = collapse(c)
		}

	}

	// sort children: directories first, then files, alphabetically
	var sortNodes func(n *node)

{"command": "cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'

open(p,'w').write(s)
# 2. file line: marker colored, name default; handle worktree-modified
p='pkg/gui/panels.go'
s=open(p).read()
start=s.index("// fileLine renders a single file line.")
end=s.index("// branchLines builds the branches panel content.")
new='''// fileLine renders a single file line.
func (gui *Gui) fileLine(name string, depth int, f *commands.StatusFile) Line {
	prefix := strings.Repeat(" ", depth*2)
	marker := ""
	var style ui.Style
	short := f.ShortStatus
	switch {
	case strings.Contains(short, "?"):
		marker = "??"
		style = ui.Style{Fg: "red"}
	case strings.Contains(short, "M"):
		marker = "M"
		style = ui.Style{Fg: "red"}
	case strings.Contains(short, "A"):
		marker = "A"
		style = ui.Style{Fg: "green"}
	case strings.Contains(short, "D"):
		marker = "D"
		style = ui.Style{Fg: "red"}
	case strings.Contains(short, "R"):
		marker = "R"
		style = ui.Style{Fg: "yellow"}
	case strings.Contains(short, "C"):
		marker = "C"
		style = ui.Style{Fg: "cyan"}
	}
	if len(marker) < 2 {
		marker = strings.Repeat(" ", 2-len(marker)) + marker
	}
	return Line{Runs: []ui.Run{
		{Text: prefix + marker, Style: style},
		{Text: " " + name, Style: ui.Style{Fg: "default"}},
	}}
}

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
# 3. main view scrollbar

# lazygit reimplementation - status report

## What works
`compile.sh` builds `./executable` (pure Go, stdlib only, no network needed).

Verified byte-identical (tmux `capture-pane -e`) against the reference binary for:
- `--help`, `--version`, `--config` (319 lines), `--print-config-dir`, invalid args/flags
- full 120x40 screens for repo1 clean, repo1 dirty (modified + untracked + subdirs),
  repo2 (remote+tags), repo3 (upstream), repo4 (120 commits), repo5..repo9
- file tree, branches, commits, stash, status, main diff views, command log,
  bottom info line, footers, scrollbars, borders/colours

Layout rules reverse-engineered:
- side width = ceil(0.3333*W); status/stash 3 rows; files/branches/commits share the
  rest; for viewHeight<=27 the *focused* panel takes the remainder, <=20 all minimums
  are 1; command log = commandLogSize+2 rows when H>=40 else 3.

## Known deviations
1. **Author colours**: the reference hashes the author name into a 256-colour index;
   the algorithm could not be recovered (tried fnv1/fnv1a(32,64), crc32, adler,
   md5/sha1/sha256/sha512, murmur3, xxh32, poly hashes, HSL->256). Mine uses
   fnv1a(name)%256 so colours differ (line 27 of the commits panel).
2. **Random tip text**: only fragments of lazygit's tip list were observed, so the
   tip list is partial; the tip is random so this is not deterministic anyway.
3. Missing: most git *actions* (commit/stash/checkout/rebase/reset/... are no-ops),
   menus other than the keybindings/extras/recent-repos popups, search filtering
   refinement, editor/subprocess integration, mouse events, i18n.

- Implement the remaining keybindings/actions in `pkg/gui/keys_app.go` +
  `pkg/gui/menus.go` (`contextKeybindings` map).
- Confirm "Disabled: No item selected" prefix rule (observed once, unreproducible).

  min(91, max(81, 1+2*floor(2W/7))) then largestOdd(W-1) - verified empirically.
- Scrollbar: lists thumb = round(inner^2/n); main view thumb =
  floor((T-1)^2/(C+T-2)+0.4) (1/36 empirical mismatch).
- Startup popup: width min(81,W-1), height min(content+2, floor(0.75*H)-1),
  y = floor((H-h)/2).
EOF
printf 'executable\n*.log\n' > .gitignore; git add -A && git commit -q -m "lazygit reimplementation" && git log --oneline | head -2"}
